title: vmblu System Configuration (v1.12.0)
description: The authored semantic and graphical description stored in a <system-name>.sys.blu file.
$comment: System context is optional. An explicitly supplied *.sys.blu path takes precedence. Otherwise, starting at the application entrypoint directory, search upward to the workspace boundary for system/active.sys.blu; the nearest match wins. Other *.sys.blu files are not implicitly active. Files and folders beside the active configuration have no implicit meaning: prompts, contracts, documentation, and other material must remain explicit references in the sysblu document.

nodes.description: vmblu and non-vmblu applications inside the modeled system boundary.

connections.description: Architecturally meaningful communication channels between system nodes.

references.description: Project-level documentation and navigation references for the system.

Header.description: Identity and lifecycle metadata for the system configuration.

Node.description: An application or system participant. The vmblu flag controls whether it is rendered as a vmblu application.

vmblu.description: True when this participant is a vmblu application; false for a non-vmblu participant.

endpoints.description: Named API or protocol attachment points rendered on the system node.

Endpoint.description: A named API or protocol attachment point on a system node.

role.description: The node's role in the API or protocol. More specialized roles may be added as real systems require them.

protocol.description: Optional path, ARL, or absolute HTTP(S) URL of a protocol definition; relative targets resolve from this system configuration.

Connection.description: One independently meaningful transport binding between endpoints.

transport.description: Explicit transport used by this binding, such as websocket, https, udp, ipc, in-process, queue, file, shared-store, other, or unspecified.

route.description: Optional intermediate points used to draw the connection.

Reference.description: A typed navigation target. Targets may be paths resolved relative to the system configuration, absolute ARLs, or absolute HTTP(S) URLs.

command.description: Terminal command requested by Ctrl/Cmd-click. Sysblu passes this string to the host without interpreting it.

workingDirectory.description: Working directory for command execution, resolved relative to this system configuration.

View.description: Presentation state for the single initial system view.

Extensions.description: Explicit namespace for vendor-specific or experimental data.
